newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas remains firm on SW heat, futures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas remains firm on SW heat, futures.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices remained firm Tuesday as hot, humid weather continued in the Southwest and the futures market staged an early rally, market sources said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices were quoted unchanged at $2.12-2.14 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub, as temperatures still hovered in the 90s F.
"It (cash) had strength at the end when the NYMEX went up," one trader said.
NYMEX's August Henry Hub natgas futures rose to a high of $2.14, up 7.2 cents from Monday.
The western market continued to keep supplies tight as the 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in California was expected to remain off line until late next week.
The adjacent unit 3, with a generating capacity of 1,080 MW, was slated to restart July 12, according to the company.

As a result of the tight capacity and stronger futures market, Permian prices edged up one cent to about $1.99-2.05. Southern California border prices also rose an average of three cents to $2.19-2.22.
San Juan prices remained firm in the low-to-mid $1.90s for constrained gas, traders said.
In the East, swing prices at the New York city-gate did not budge from the mid-to-high $2.30s as moderate weather in the region created only minimal demand.

In the Midwest, swing prices were about one cent higher at $1.99-2.00. Chicago city-gate was also talked little changed around $2.16-2.17 as temperature highs were forecast in the low-to-mid 70s F in the region.
